question: Where do the organisms that cause endogenous reproductive tract infections primarily come from?

options.A: Bacterial contamination from improperly sterilized surgical tools
options.B: Microbes that already live naturally inside the vagina
options.C: Waterborne parasites acquired from swimming in stagnant pools
options.D: Pathogens transmitted exclusively through sexual intercourse

explanation: Endogenous infections happen when microbes that normally live inside the vagina start to overgrow because the local environment changes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it helpful to know the difference between an endogenous infection and a sexually transmitted infection (STI)?

options.A: Only sexually transmitted infections can cause visible changes in vaginal discharge
options.B: Only STIs cause symptoms that result in psychological distress for the patient
options.C: Endogenous infections are always permanent while STIs can be easily cured
options.D: Endogenous infections do not typically require routine partner treatment like STIs do

explanation: Knowing an infection is endogenous saves the patient from unnecessary blame or partner tracing, since these issues come from internal balance shifts rather than outside transmission. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which helpful bacteria group is mostly responsible for keeping the vaginal environment healthy and acidic?
explanation: Lactobacilli are the good bacteria that dominate a healthy vagina. They produce lactic acid to keep the pH low and protect against harmful overgrowth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h2)

question: What happens to the vaginal pH when the number of protective Lactobacilli drops a lot?

options.A: It remains perfectly stable because the cervix regulates the pH
options.B: It shifts entirely to a neutral balance that supports normal tissue repair
options.C: It becomes extremely acidic, killing off all bacteria completely
options.D: It becomes less acidic, which encourages harmful microbes to grow

explanation: When lactic acid goes down, the vaginal pH rises above 4.5. This creates an easy environment for bad microbes to multiply. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which common practice washes away protective bacteria and raises vaginal pH?
explanation: Douching disrupts the natural balance by washing away helpful Lactobacilli and introducing fluids that neutralize vaginal acidity. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h3)

question: How can taking broad-spectrum antibiotics lead to yeast infections or bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: By changing the systemic blood pressure of the reproductive organs
options.B: By increasing the production of glycogen in the vaginal walls
options.C: By killing protective Lactobacilli alongside harmful bacteria
options.D: By directly stimulating the rapid growth of yeast and anaerobic microbes

explanation: Antibiotics wipe out the friendly bacteria that normally keep other microbes in check, leaving an open path for overgrowth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h3)

question: What kind of vaginal discharge is most typical for a yeast infection (vulvovaginal candidiasis)?

options.A: Thick, white, and curdy like cottage cheese
options.C: Thin, gray-white with a strong fishy odor

explanation: Yeast infections usually show up with a thick, white, cottage cheese-like discharge along with severe itching and irritation. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h4)

question: A patient has a thin gray vaginal discharge and a noticeable fishy odor that gets worse after sex. What is the most likely condition?
explanation: A thin gray discharge with a fishy smell, especially when semen makes the odor stronger, points directly to bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h4)

question: What finding under a microscope is a key sign of bacterial vaginosis?
explanation: Clue cells are vaginal skin cells covered in so many bacteria that their edges look fuzzy and unclear, which points to bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h5)

question: During a speculum exam, why do midwives perform a whiff test using 10 percent potassium hydroxide?

options.A: To stain the bacterial cell walls for easy microscopic counting
options.B: To measure the exact acidity level of the vaginal walls
options.C: To kill off unwanted parasites before collecting laboratory samples
options.D: To release volatile amines that produce a distinct fishy odor

explanation: Potassium hydroxide reacts with the chemical byproducts of bacterial overgrowth, releasing a strong fishy smell that helps confirm bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which medication is commonly given first to treat bacterial vaginosis?
explanation: Metronidazole is the standard first-line medicine because it works very well against the anaerobic bacteria causing bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is treating male sexual partners usually NOT needed when a woman is treated for bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Clinical trials show partner treatment does not prevent the infection from returning
options.B: The medications used to treat women are completely toxic to male physiology
options.C: Bacterial vaginosis is strictly genetic and has nothing to do with microbial transfer
options.D: Men cannot carry the anaerobic bacteria that cause this specific condition

explanation: Because bacterial vaginosis is an internal shift in normal vaginal flora rather than a classic sexually transmitted infection, treating the partner does not stop it from coming back. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h6)

question: What serious pregnancy complication is strongly linked to untreated bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Complete cessation of fetal growth throughout the third trimester
options.B: Severe maternal hypertension and sudden eclamptic fits
options.C: Complete placental detachment during the first trimester
options.D: Preterm labor and premature rupture of membranes

explanation: Enzymes produced by bad bacteria can weaken the bag of waters and trigger early contractions, which can lead to preterm birth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h7)

question: What condition can a newborn baby get after passing through a birth canal affected by a maternal yeast infection?
explanation: Babies can pick up Candida yeast during a vaginal birth, which often shows up as white patches inside their mouth called oral thrush. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h7)

question: What type of underwear fabric is best to help prevent recurring vaginal infections?
explanation: Cotton breathes well and absorbs moisture, helping prevent the warm, damp conditions where yeast and anaerobic bacteria love to grow. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h8)

question: Which of these practices should a midwife actively advise women against during vaginal hygiene counseling?

options.A: Washing the external vulva gently with clean water and mild soap
options.B: Drying the external genital area thoroughly after taking a bath
options.C: Using antiseptics or soapy water to douche inside the vagina
options.D: Promptly changing menstrual pads every few hours during flow

explanation: Internal douching washes away protective bacteria and changes the pH, making the vagina much more vulnerable to infections. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h8)
